title: The Partner Manager's Co-Sell Workflow With 5 PartnerStack Skills
summary: Fit five AI Skills into your week to keep your co-sell workflow on track.
body_markdown:
A competitive advantage is good. An advantage over your competitors that feels almost unfair is better. And that’s what the Skills in our[Partner Skills Marketplace](https://skills.partnerstack.com/) are built to help with.


These AI Skills are purpose-built for partner programs and curated by PartnerStack and the community, including experienced partnership professionals who’ve built and shared their own workflows.


One of those contributors is[Chris Lavoie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chris-lavoie-phd-aaaa4111b) , Founder and CEO at Partnership Mastermind, who has[authored 10 Skills](https://skills.partnerstack.com/authors/19) on the marketplace. We asked him how he structures a partner manager’s week, then mapped five Skills from our team and community onto that rhythm for your[co-sell](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/co-selling) workflow.


## A Skill is the playbook that plays for you


A Skill gives an AI assistant — like Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini — a reusable set of instructions for how to handle a specific task. That makes a Skill a lot like a playbook, except it can actually run the plays for you.


Lavoie has seen that shift firsthand. “I was doing playbooks for a long time, and then the AI era came about, and playbooks started to collect dust a bit and look a little bit like the way of the dinosaur… A playbook is like this static document. The second you publish it, it's immediately stale and outdated.”


He adds, “The beauty of a Skill is that it makes it so much more agile and adaptable. A user can say, ‘Hey, I want to do this for a particular thing.’ And then your Claude \[can\] say, ‘Oh, you actually have access to this PartnerStack Skill. Do you want to use it?’ Okay, yes. And then it puts it on dummy-proof autopilot.”


## Skill 1: Weekly Partner Actions & Digest for Monday triage


In general, Lavoie advises time boxing for a partner manager workflow. He likes to front-load his week with tasks that will require action from someone else.


“I like to index the early part of my week on things that just take time to develop,” he says. “Like, you're trying to build a pipeline. What are some things that you need to get in motion on a Monday that you would regret if you waited till Thursday or Friday?”


He adds that most of those tasks are things that require external steps or other people’s feedback. “You're waiting on a partner to do something very specific. Well, it's like, realistically, if I message them, it's going to take them 24 to 48 hours to respond.” So, he gets those tasks started on Monday or Tuesday, giving them time to “simmer and percolate.”


To see what needs attention first, start the week with the[Weekly Partner Actions & Digest](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/weekly-partner-actions-digest) , built by PartnerStack’s Adam Steinberg. It pulls real-time PartnerStack data into a prioritized action list covering:


- Pending applications, scored and ranked so likely fraud or test accounts are flagged
- Commissions that need review
- Stalled or expiring deals
- Partners gone dark
- Wins to acknowledge
- Rising partners worth investing in


Each item comes with a one-click action, so you can work through your weekly queue in one sitting.


For newly approved partners, or ones who’ve gone dark, Lavoie’s[Partner Onboarding Activation Skill](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/partner-onboarding-activation-skill) builds a 30-60-90 activation plan aimed at their first sourced or influenced deal.


## Skill 2: Partner Pipeline Digest for the revenue review


[Partner Pipeline Digest](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/partner-pipeline-digest) , built by William Chin, connects to Salesforce, HubSpot or Looker and turns your open partner deals into a Monday morning digest.


It separates:


- [Partner-sourced](https://partnerstack.com/articles/your-guide-to-determining-who-gets-credit-for-a-co-sell-deal) deals that a partner brought in
- Partner-influenced deals that a partner helped move forward


It groups pipeline by partner tier, region and type (such as referral, reseller, SI or ISV) and ranks partners by how much pipeline they contribute. This partner pipeline review can help you define your next actions, while flagging stale deals.


Lavoie knows the value of that kind of view. On PartnerStack’s[Get It, Together podcast](https://partnerstack.com/podcast-episodes/building-partnership-programs-that-scale) , he described the top-of-funnel-down dashboards he built for his partnerships team: “Any partner manager on my team could log in and be like, okay, I’ve added this many leads this quarter, this many have converted into deals. This is how much active pipeline I have right now.”


## Skill 3: Partner Pipeline Quality Audit for investment decisions


Are partners bringing you good sales opportunities? The[Partner Pipeline Quality Audit](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/partner-pipeline-quality-audit) , built by PartnerStack CMO Tyler Calder, helps answer that question by scoring partner deals across:


- **ICP fit:** Does the customer match your[ideal customer profile](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/ideal-customer-profile-icp) ?
- **Win rate:** How often do the partner’s deals become sales?
- **Velocity:** How quickly do deals move through the sales process?
- **Average ACV:** What’s the average annual contract value?
- **Retention:** Do those customers stay after buying?


You can run it through the PartnerStack MCP, your CRM, a file upload or a guided interview. You’ll get an audit report with recommendations you can bring to leadership.


This will help you separate the partners creating qualified pipeline from the partners creating volume. That distinction matters: on the[Get It, Together podcast](https://partnerstack.com/podcast-episodes/building-partnership-programs-that-scale) , Lavoie pointed out that goals like “add 10 SQLs this quarter” let partner managers “off the hook of focusing and obsessing over the quality.”


*See more:*[Deep-funnel affiliate metrics: How enterprise SaaS teams measure success](https://partnerstack.com/articles/affiliate-program-metrics) *.*


## Skill 4: Co-Sell Deal Brief before every joint customer call


Before any joint call with a partner and a live prospect, the[Co-Sell Deal Brief](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/co-sell-deal-brief) , built by Bluethread.io’s Rob Moyer, gives you a one-screen brief.


It starts with a “Primary Sale” check: evidence that the partner’s rep is personally committed to the deal. Then it covers:


- The joint value story
- Call roles
- The deal’s state (green, yellow or red)
- The most likely three-party issue, and how to head it off


Co-sell calls have three parties, and most sales methods are built for two. This brief is designed to fill that gap.


*Related:*[Co-sell rules of engagement: what to include (and what most teams miss)](https://partnerstack.com/articles/co-sell-rules-of-engagement) *.*


## Skill 5: Find Partner Enablement Gaps for the Friday feedback loop


End the week by looking at what’s holding partners back.[Find Partner Enablement Gaps](https://skills.partnerstack.com/skills/find-partner-enablement-gaps) , built by PartnerStack’s Taylor Kendrick, helps identify what partners are missing or what’s getting in their way.


The Skill looks for four types of problems:


- **Coverage:** Enablement doesn’t exist, but should
- **Completion:** Enablement exists, but partners aren’t using it
- **Quality:** Partners use the enablement, but it isn’t working
- **Access:** Some partner segments can’t get to the enablement


This helps you connect training, resource use and support patterns to performance. You’ll get a prioritized list of fixes, along with what’s working and shouldn’t change, to feed into next week’s plan.


*You might also like:*[What great partner enablement looks like in co-sell](https://partnerstack.com/articles/partner-enablement-co-sell) *.*


## Put the five Skills into one weekly co-sell cadence


Here’s what your co-sell workflow could look like for an average week:


- **Monday:** Triage the program and inspect pipeline (e.g., Weekly Partner Actions & Digest, Partner Pipeline Digest)
- **Tuesday to Thursday:** Audit quality and prepare active deals (e.g., Partner Pipeline Quality Audit, Co-Sell Deal Brief)
- **Friday:** Close out actions and feed enablement gaps into next week’s plan (e.g., Find Partner Enablement Gaps)


## What the partner manager should not delegate


What still needs the human touch? What tasks should AI not handle?


Even for the work you hand off, don’t take AI’s output at face value. Lavoie recommends one simple step to calibrate your tools first.


He advises asking, “Hey, Chat or Claude, based on what you understand for this job to be done, and based on these data sources you have access to, tell me how you understand my operating reality. What do you see when you look into our HubSpot? What do you see when you look into these different data sources?”


He says adding this level of calibration and refinement to AI partner management is like giving someone a pair of glasses to see better.


“That simple step I just described has probably been the biggest unlock for me on the AI front, because we just kind of blindly trust that AI knows exactly what it's doing.”


Beyond that, the human touch is still required on some tasks, including:


- Relationship judgment
- Escalation
- Commercial commitments
- Partner feedback


You should also still personally investigate incomplete or contradictory data.


*See also:*[Dos and don’ts of using AI for your partner program in 2027](https://partnerstack.com/articles/ai-dos-and-donts) *.*


## Ensure your workflow is actually tighter


Never mistake activity for accomplishment. You may be actively using your new Skills, but do they have a real impact?


### Track time saved, action completion, stale-deal reduction and preparation coverage


Use today’s numbers as a starting point, then ask yourself:


- What is your weekly review time?
- Which tasks were finished on time, and which spilled over?


This is how you ensure your PartnerStack Skills are actually paying off.


### Track pipeline quality, deal progression, partner activation and enablement outcomes


Pay special attention to whether:


- Your deals are better-matched moving forward, and they’re closing
- Your new partners bring in their first deal
- Your enablement fixes help partners work more effectively


These results show whether your partner manager workflow improves partner operations.

## Co-sell workflow FAQs


### What is a co-sell workflow?


A co-sell workflow gives you and your partners repeatable steps and responsibilities to work a sale.


### How do PartnerStack Skills work with the PartnerStack MCP?


Skills give your AI instructions.[Our PartnerStack MCP](https://partnerstack.com/platform/mcp) connects it to your account information and supported actions. Additional connections, like your CRM, may be required.


### Which PartnerStack Skills help with pipeline reviews?


Partner Pipeline Digest shows your partner-sourced and partner-influenced deals. Partner Pipeline Quality Audit can assess whether those opportunities are a good fit and lead to sales.


### What co-sell decisions should remain human-led?


People are still at the heart of making the decisions about:


- Relationships
- Pricing promises
- Partner investment
- Sensitive problems and escalations
- Partner feedback
- Approving changes or messages
